text: Thoughts on KOD? So I left the Cole show, and decided run though his entire discography start to finish, ending with TFO. Then got to KOD. Now mind you, when KOD dropped, yeah of course I enjoyed it. It’s Cole. But I remember thinking this album is his personal worst. The peak being 2014, then 4YEO: loved it, but felt it didn’t top the album before. But yet some of my favorite songs are on there (self titled). When KOD released, I felt disappointed. While I felt like it wasn’t a bad record at all, it wasn’t as good as 4YEO. And hell no, not in the same lane as 2014. Now, maybe it’s because I don’t listen to hip hop much anymore, I felt like KOD aged well. Especially the concept. Kids born in the system, either the streets or a rapper or ball player. The kids choosing the streets. Drugs become fun to a way to escape and eventually to downfall. KOD is aging like fine wine to me.

text: Safety hits me so hard man I know a lot of people here can probably relate to getting a text message, looking down at your phone and it's from someone you were close to bringing bad news. As I get older I see those moments get closer and closer to each other. And at some point you kinda start expecting it, or have an off feeling all day long and then you're just hit with a text that you know will just affect you mentally for a long ass while. Cole wraps this feeling up in such a melancholy, somber way. And there's a slight charm of this moment being from your hometown while you're far away, it's such a specific message. I always loved this man's music, he's really good at delivering little specific feelings like this and it just hits you sometimes whether or not you relate to them.
